newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S TABLE MOUNTAIN IN 74 MLN RAND UPGRADE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S TABLE MOUNTAIN IN 74 MLN RAND UPGRADE.

text.p: One of South Africa's premier tourist attractions, Table Mountain dominating Cape Town's skyline, is set to undergo a 74 million rand revamp.

The project aims to upgrade the cableway that this year took 450,000 people up the mountain, installing new cablecars and construct a new water reservoir and restaurant, transforming the current restaurant into an information centre.

"It will be a visual spectacle. This has all been brought about because of the queues and the lack of facilities at the top of the mountain," Table Mountain Aerial Cableway Company managing director John Harrison told Reuters.
He said that the cableway would be closed on January 12, when construction would start in earnest under the eagle eyes of environmentalists.
The project is expected to be completed by October 1,1997.
Already a crane has been erected on the mountain, site offices and accommodation for about 50 workers have been set up and the helicopter landing site identified.
Harrison said that the mountain top would resemble "a typical construction site" but that all efforts would be made not to harm the national monument in any way.
"It is an environmentally sensitive area and we will have everybody watching us," he said.

The new Swiss-made cablecars would increase the number of people that can be taken up the mountain on each trip to 65 from the present 25, which will mean that 900 people could be ferried up each hour compared to the present 230.
The cablecars will have revolving floors and will give passengers a 360 degree view of the mountain and the city.
